body.subject: Issue #314 lane 3: a bridge session survives a resident reincarnation - one rediscovery, ONE typed notification, and a once-replayed in-flight call

items.change: BatonWebApplicationFacade takes a rebind authority (4th constructor option {rediscover, incarnation}); openBatonWebConnection is the ONE exported derivation the open path and the rebind share (discovery + doctor + session + the incarnation the connection names), and connectBatonWebApplication wires it unless the caller handed an explicit connection (an embedder with no publication to re-read keeps today's behavior exactly). A facade built without one (every existing 3-arg construction) is byte-identical to before.
items.evidence: 314e-l3-a: a real resident + a staged handoff; the successor was discovered once (/v1/application-card requested exactly once) and the next call answered from it

items.change: The rebind fires on FACTS, never a timer: _rebindableFailure (the stale-incarnation refusal #306 and the web transport's own refusal from a dispatch, never a request that outlived its own bound) and _incarnationGone (a failed transport, or the resident naming its own stop - the #316 b typed end). The plane reports both its ends (including a refused reconnect) and every frame it delivered before any subscription filter judges it.
items.evidence: 314e-l3-b drives the dispatch trigger with NO wake subscription; 314e-l3-a drives the plane trigger (the old's SSE leg ends resident_stopping at the handoff)

items.change: The incarnation_changed wake class is a second, independent trigger: frame.row.payloadKind host.reincarnated starts a rebind, and the #306r arm is respected by construction - host.reincarnation_failed means the predecessor re-took its authority and the publication still names it, so there is no successor to bind to, no rediscovery and no notification. The handoff class is deliberately NOT contact (a replayed host.reincarnated after the rebind must not mint a second handoff).
items.evidence: 314e-l3-d: the real 306r window (the successor dies between its marker and its publication) delivers the failure row to the subscription, then 0 rediscoveries, no notification, the publication still the old incarnation, and doctor() still answering

items.change: _sessionAuthority(current, {rebind}) is the ONE re-attestation: same userId, a superset of the bound capabilities, the same repoId, not revoked, a parsable future expiry - and the resident-issued sessionId is the ONE axis the rebind re-binds (the resident mints it per incarnation, SessionStore.issue at open). The frozen client-facing principal is never mutated, so validPrincipal and the derived mutation key are unchanged across a handoff. A successor whose session narrows the grant refuses application_unauthorized and the session ends typed (no further rebind attempts).
items.evidence: 314e-l3-a: my rediscover double answers a session that re-mints only the sessionId; the rebind adopts it, and the dispatch 30 lines later still attests against the same principal

items.change: ONE notifications/baton/resident_reincarnated per handoff: the facade composes the frame kind baton.resident_reincarnated {from, to, cursor, at} (from/to are the incarnations AND the resident sessions the connection named), the plane announces it whatever any subscription filter admits (announce() uses the session's own delivery sink, once however many subscriptions are open), and mcp-northbound.mjs spells the METHOD beside WAKE_NOTIFICATION_METHOD and routes by frame kind.
items.evidence: 314e-l3-a asserts exactly one frame, from.incarnation === the old publication, to.incarnation === receipt.successor.incarnation; 314e-l3-e asserts the method list [notifications/baton/wake, notifications/baton/resident_reincarnated]

items.change: The client swap happens between dispatches: the successor's client replaces the old only AFTER its session is attested, the dispatch attestation is dropped (it belonged to the old client), and the wake plane re-opens through the new client via a new reopen() with its subscription records and its _cursor untouched. When the rediscovery finds nothing reachable, the plane gets its OWN bounded cadence back (resume()) instead of a tight re-attach loop.
items.evidence: 314e-l3-c: a subscription opened before the handoff still delivers after it with the SAME subscriptionId, and the re-attached stream names last-event-id equal to the cursor the session had reached

items.change: _onceAfterRebind wraps the dispatches and the reads a dead transport can meet (command, doctor, actionAuthority, authorizeReplay, wakeSince) and replays ONCE after an adopted rebind; the idempotency key is derived before it, so a mutation crosses the boundary under the SAME key and a second failure propagates as the refusal it is. The wrappers stay async, so a synchronous refusal is still a rejection (the mcp-bridge-admission rows pin that).
items.evidence: 314e-l3-b: with no wake subscription, a mutation issued after the handoff is retried against the successor under the same key - both attempts carry ONE derived key (new Set(keys).size === 1), the successor ledger holds one row, and repeating the same call replays that row

items.change: docs/49 section 6 carries a Landed note naming the three recorded deltas (the rebind authority derivation, the ONE trigger classification with the #306r reading, the once-retry); docs/48 section 11 gains item 15 naming the bridge's rebind beside the handoff rows; the two manifest rows this lane turned green (314-e1, 314-e2) are retired, canonically re-rendered. seam-inventory and surface-gate regenerate with no delta (mcp-web-bridge.mjs is not a tracked seam file; the gate is ok).

carriedForward: THE BRIEF'S VERIFY SET NAMES TWO FILES THAT DO NOT EXIST: impl/test/issue270-*.test.mjs and impl/test/issue294-*.test.mjs match nothing in this checkout (the runner refuses a nonexistent path as an unexpected failure). The #270 admission rows live in test/mcp-bridge-admission.test.mjs and the #294 wake-consumer rows in test/wake-mcp-consumers.test.mjs; both were run (green) in their place.

THE REBIND LATCH IS SEMANTIC, NOT TEMPORAL: a successor that is already bound is not re-bound until the session has been back in contact with it (a delivered frame that is not the handoff class, or any successful dispatch). This is what makes ONE rediscovery per handoff hold against a plane that keeps re-attaching. A reviewer should read it as the design decision it is: the alternative (a second rediscovery per end) is what the design's ONE-notification law cannot survive.

A DOWN resident is re-discovered by the plane's OWN cadence: when the publication names no successor (the old is down, or the #306r arm re-published), each failed re-attach attempts one rediscovery (3 file reads + a failing socket connect) bounded by the client's pollMs - never a second timer constant. That is also the recovery path for a watch-only session: a successor published while the session is stranded is found without any dispatch. A reviewer who wants that polled less often should move the cadence, not add a latch.

The successor's CARD IS ADOPTED WHOLESALE on a rebind (commands, registry digest), as the rediscover answer the design mints; a reincarnation to a different commit serves a different registry, and refusing it (the fresh-open digest check) would make every such reincarnation fatal to a live session. The authority axes the design does pin (userId, the grant, the repoId) are judged exactly, and a narrowed grant ends the session typed.

The file's own 4th-arg option is {rediscover, incarnation}: the design pinned rediscover's answer as {client, card, session}, and the incarnation rides it as the fourth fact (without it, from/to would be a digest restated by hand). e1/e2 in the design red file construct the facade with only {rediscover} and stay green - the fallback is the sessionId pair.
needsFromOthers: impl/src/index.mjs (outside this lane's path scope): openBatonWebConnection is deliberately NOT re-exported from the package entry (mcp-web-bridge.mjs already exports boundWakePage/WakeSubscriptions/kimiBaton* without an entry row, so nothing is inconsistent today). A lane that owns index.mjs and wants the rebind authority reachable from the package surface adds ONE row beside connectBatonWebApplication.

docs/39-swarm-runtime.md (a docs-scoped lane, out of scope here): its wake section (Waking the orchestrator) should name the bridge's own session-lifecycle notification - notifications/baton/resident_reincarnated, emitted once per handoff and routed by frame kind beside notifications/baton/wake - and that a bridge session re-binds to the successor rather than dying with the incarnation (docs/49 section 6 and docs/48 section 11 item 15 carry the landed truth until then).

impl/src/swarm-contract.mjs (out of scope): the baton_wakes tool description could teach that the session emits notifications/baton/resident_reincarnated when the resident reincarnates under it, so a client that sees an unfamiliar method has the contract at the tool schema and not only in docs/49 section 6.5.
